Subject: Post-demo recommended model shortlist + rationale

Hi Alex / Priya,

We completed an initial set of evals on the prompt set and labeled intents you uploaded. Below is a prioritized shortlist with rationale, preliminary quality numbers, and cost/latency estimates. Full results and logs are attached and linked.

Shortlist (recommended order):
1) Redwood-14B-Opt (4-bit) — Recommended primary for intent classification
   - Why: Best balance of throughput and F1 on your labeled set. 95th p latency @ 128-token inference is ~120ms on our Dedicated profile; estimated per-token cost ~0.004 USD for your traffic pattern.
   - Tradeoffs: Slightly lower abstractive summary richness vs larger models but much more economical at scale.

2) Mistral-Instruct-32B (int8) — Recommended for high-quality summarization and assistant (mid-cost)
   - Why: Highest ROUGE-L and factuality scores on the 3k prompt set; better hallucination control on our factuality probes. Latency ~240–300ms for 512-token summaries on Dedicated; cost ~0.012 USD/token equivalent given your batch sizes.
   - Tradeoffs: Higher cost and latency; reserve for flows where quality is critical.

3) Open-7B-4bit (distilled) — Inexpensive baseline for prototyping and high-QPS intent routing
   - Why: Lowest cost per inference; 95th p latency ~80ms; per-token cost ~0.0015 USD. Accuracy on intent classification is acceptable for deterministic routing, but F1 lags Redwood-14B on ambiguous queries.
   - Tradeoffs: Noticeable quality gap on ambiguous/edge-case queries and longer summarizations. Not recommended for the final assistant experience.

Notes on long-context runs and monitoring:
- Long context: We tested Redwood-14B-Opt at 16k tokens for the assistant flows. Quality improves for long-document summarization, but median latency increased ~1.8x. See attached "model_shortlist_cost_latency.csv" for per-config numbers.
- Regression monitoring: Recommend nightly synthetic re-runs of the 3k prompt set against the production model tag. Trigger thresholds: ROUGE-L drop >3 points or intent F1 drop >2.5% -> rollback/canary.
- Pilot plan: Canary Redwood-14B-Opt for intent routing (10% traffic), Mistral-Instruct-32B for high-value summarization. Auto-fallback to Open-7B on capacity pressure.

Attachments: acme_eval_benchmarks_q2.xlsx (results), acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl, model_shortlist_cost_latency.csv

Related links: https://redwood-inference.app/drive/acme-eval-results (detailed results), HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/DEAL-89321

Questions ahead of Wednesday:
- Do these recommendations align with your cost targets? If yes, we'll scope a Dedicated monthly commit + burst plan.
- Any compliance/hosting constraints for the assistant route that would push you to Private deployment?

Happy to walk through the numbers live.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
